title.title: Rebuilding a function field from its Milnor K-theory
title.subtitle: Claim: a function field of dimension $\ge 2$ is recovered from its mod-$\ell$ Milnor K-groups $K_1$, $K_2$

d.label: maps of the degree 1 and 2 data

beats.text: Recover a field $K$ over an algebraically closed field from mod-$\ell$ data in degrees 1 and 2
That the data pin down at most one field map is formalized
That every compatible map of the data comes from a field map is not

achievement.label: Bogomolov's program (1991)
achievement.context: Before: known over algebraic closures of finite fields (Bogomolov–Tschinkel, Pop); open over e.g. $\mathbb{C}$
achievement.note: Up to perfect closure and Frobenius twists; transcendence degree $\ge 2$

verify.detail: In Lean: injectivity only. The reconstruction itself is not formalized
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean docs and allowed axioms; we did not build it

sources.quote: Bogomolov-Tschinkel proved reconstruction for function fields over algebraic closures of finite fields
Over general algebraically closed constants (e.g. C) the full conjecture was open.

A function field K of transcendence degree >= 2 over an algebraically closed field (characteristic != l) is recovered, up to perfect closure and Frobenius twists, from K_1^M/l, K_2^M/l and the Milnor product alone
The Lean covers the easy direction (injectivity). The headline Milnor K reconstruction (existence/surjectivity) is not formalized.
only `propext`, `Quot.sound` and `Classical.choice` for every family here

plain: A big number system is rebuilt from a small table of how its elements multiply, like a skeleton from bones

steps: Record which pairs of elements multiply to zero in degree two
Those pairs trace out lines, as in projective geometry
Lines and valuations rebuild the field itself

data.result: the field, up to Frobenius twists

voice.text: Degree one and two data should pin down the field. Uniqueness is in Lean.
Products that vanish trace out lines, and lines rebuild the field.
Claimed: the field comes back, up to Frobenius.
